## Review scope and decisions

**Priority finding:** LTFM departures in September 2024 lack 40 NM crossing times
for **65.87%** of observations and 100 NM crossing times for **61.58%**, throughout
the month. Both the original reference inputs and current archive show the gap.
This requires a reference-period coverage review before clearing representativeness.

Two additional support issues merit review: LFPG departure use of reference groups
with fewer than 20 observations reaches **8.94%** in August 2025; LTFM reaches
**7.58%** in February 2025 and remains elevated in 2026. These are successful
matches to thin reference samples, which a reference-miss summary alone would hide.

Across the common January–September windows, missing-crossing shares are lower in
2026 than in 2024 at every airport; there is no general deterioration on that measure.
LGAV remains near 11–12%. Runway 09 at LTFM remains the main confirmed new-reference
gap in 2026, with supplementation deferred.

This review covers the original 2024 reference inputs and the manifest-pinned
archive extracts for 2024, 2025 and January–September 2026. **2026 stops at
30 September**, despite this review being prepared in November. Full-year 2024
and 2025 summaries are retained; January–September is the common comparison
window. Available dates do not certify complete movement reporting.

The reference values, sector definitions, production eligibility and existing
additional-time outputs are unchanged. PBWG `(p05 + p15) / 2` and ICAO-labelled
`p20` use identical reference keys and sample counts, verified here; these
coverage results therefore apply to both variants.

The exception register records evidence, interpretation and next steps. Its
statuses are review decisions, not automated publication approval. No new
runway baseline has been estimated in this review.

## Read the denominators first

- **Reported observations** are airport movements expanded to 40 and 100 NM.
  Combined tables therefore count each movement twice. They are not unique-flight
  counts. Detailed tables separate arrivals/departures and each range.
- The date is the UTC movement date, falling back to block date if the movement
  time is missing. Unknown-phase, undated and out-of-window records remain in
  [the input inventory](input-inventory.csv), outside the corresponding sample.
- **Missing crossing %** uses all reported observations. Absence can reflect
  actual non-crossing or unavailable data; it is not automatically a data error.
- **Data attention %** counts the union of unidentified runway/class/airport,
  absent movement timestamp, invalid travel-time direction/duration, and missing
  bearing where a crossing time exists. Helicopter exclusion alone is not a data
  error. These flags can overlap crossing gaps and must not be added to them.
- **Reference miss %** uses algorithm-valid observations as denominator. Its
  identified and unidentified components remain separate. A valid-looking
  unmatched key is a candidate operational change, not proof of one.
- **Matched coverage %** uses all reported observations. Literal `NA` runway
  categories retain current production behavior: some match diagnostic reference
  cells. Their counts are disclosed separately; matching does not establish that
  the operational subgroup is identified.
- **Sparse-reference exposure %** uses matched observations as denominator.
  Cells with fewer than 5 or 20 reference observations are retained. Twenty is a
  design target, not an enforced eligibility threshold.

Screening bands are **LOW <2%; WATCH 2–<5%; REVIEW 5–<10%; SUBSTANTIAL ≥10%**.
They draw attention to rates, with no automatic pass/fail. A small annual rate
can conceal a material local episode. Expected non-crossings need explanation,
not forced matching or imputation. All percentages below are calculated from
summed counts, never averages of subgroup percentages.

## 2024 reference release summary

This uses the original reference-building extracts. Zero in-sample reference
misses are expected and do not establish adequacy on their own. Coverage,
diagnostic categories and sparse-cell exposure still require review. The saved
release status is `COVERAGE_REVIEW_PENDING`, a new coverage-review status rather
than a revocation of the existing reference run.

```{r}
tab(release |> transmute(Airport=ICAO, `Reported × range`=N_REPORTED,
  `Matched %`=PCT_MATCHED_REPORTED, `Crossing absent %`=PCT_MISSING_CROSSING,
  `Data attention %`=PCT_DATA_ATTENTION, Groups=N_REFERENCE_GROUPS,
  `Groups N<20`=N_GROUPS_LT20, `Exposure N<20 %`=PCT_SMALL_REF_20_MATCHED))
```

## Comparable January–September trends

### Missing crossing time

```{r}
trend <- function(field) {
 jansep |> select(ICAO,YEAR,all_of(field)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=YEAR, values_from=all_of(field)) |>
  mutate(`2026 − 2024 (pp)`=.data[["2026"]]-.data[["2024"]]) |> rename(Airport=ICAO)
}
tab(trend("PCT_MISSING_CROSSING"))
```

### Data-attention flags

```{r}
tab(trend("PCT_DATA_ATTENTION"))
```

### Missing reference among valid observations

```{r}
tab(trend("PCT_MISS_VALID"), digits=3)
```

### Exposure to reference groups with fewer than 20 observations

```{r}
tab(trend("PCT_SMALL_REF_20_MATCHED"))
```

## Exception register

```{r}
tab(exceptions |> select(ID=EXCEPTION_ID,Airport=AIRPORT,Issue=TITLE,Status=STATUS))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
for (i in seq_len(nrow(exceptions))) {
 e <- exceptions[i,]
 cat("\n### ",e$EXCEPTION_ID," — ",e$TITLE,"\n\n",sep="")
 cat("**Scope:** ",e$AIRPORT,"; ",e$PERIOD,". **Status:** ",e$STATUS,".\n\n",sep="")
 cat(e$EVIDENCE,"\n\n",e$INTERPRETATION,"\n\n",sep="")
 cat("**Treatment and next step:** ",e$ACTION,"\n\n",sep="")
 cat("Evidence: ",e$SOURCE,"\n\n",sep="")
}
```

[Download the exception register](exception-register.csv). Entries distinguish
observations from causal explanations; review dates and ownership can be added
when individual issues are assigned.

## Verification and provenance

```{r}
tab(checks)
```

Source object/member paths, upstream metadata and verified MD5 values are retained
in [sources.csv](sources.csv). The pinned [upstream manifest](upstream-apdf-manifest.csv),
[reference run manifest](reference-run-manifest.csv), [code hashes](code-and-method.csv),
[session information](session-info.txt) and [input inventory](input-inventory.csv)
make the review traceable. MD5 checks transfer consistency, not authenticity.

The [source-vintage comparison](reference-source-vintage-comparison.csv) shows
**zero differences** in the six checked count measures for all 52 original-versus-
archived 2024 airport/phase/range cells. This is aggregate coverage agreement,
not a claim that every source field or identifier is unchanged.

The current archived 2024 extract is deliberately separate from the original
reference-input cohort. Any differences are treated as source-vintage effects
until investigated. Temporal comparisons use the same archive snapshot across
2024–2026; references remain those built from the original 2024 inputs.

See also the [ASMA/DSMA technical note](../../inst/TN-XSMA.html#sec-reference-applicability)
for the LTFM and LGAV case studies.
